info.title: Print.App API
info.description: Server-to-server API for Print.App integrations: designs and their page content, folders, files, fonts, palettes, product assignments, projects and editor links. Authenticate every request with a secret key: `Authorization: Bearer sk_…`. Never call it from a browser.

tags.name: Account
tags.description: The account a secret key belongs to.

tags.name: Designs
tags.description: The designs (templates) your customers start from: create them at a size, manage their pages, and place text, images and shapes on them.

tags.name: Design folders
tags.description: Folders that organise your designs. A design can sit in more than one folder.

tags.name: Files
tags.description: Your own images and graphics, used in designs and offered to customers in the editor.

tags.name: Graphic folders
tags.description: Folders of files, shown in the editor under Pictures, Backgrounds, Textures or Frames.

tags.name: Fonts
tags.description: The fonts your designs and customers can use: the built-in set, imported Google fonts and fonts you upload.

tags.name: Palettes
tags.description: Colour palettes offered in the editor.

tags.name: Products
tags.description: Which designs open for each product (and variant) in your store.

tags.name: Links
tags.description: Shareable editor links that open a design or project at create.print.app.

post.description:
Adds, changes and removes text, images, shapes, frames, QR codes and other items on a design's pages, as one batch of operations. The batch is checked against the operation schemas first and refused as a whole if any operation is malformed (400). It then runs in order; if any operation fails, nothing is saved (422). With `dryRun: true` it runs without saving.

Place images and SVG graphics as files: upload them with `POST /v2/files` (from a URL) or `POST /v2/files/uploads`, then give the file id as `asset`. An SVG file stays vector in print. Don't send SVG markup inline (`svg`): the firewall in front of the API refuses request bodies that carry markup, with an HTML 403.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Makes a retry safe: a second request with the same key and the same body gets the first response back (for 24 hours) instead of creating the resource again. Use a new key, such as a UUID, for every new request.

RequestId.description: Identifies the request. Quote it when contacting support.

IdempotentReplayed.description: `true` when the response is the stored answer to an earlier request with the same Idempotency-Key.

ContentItem.title: ContentItem
ContentItem.description: One item on a page. Target it in `POST /v2/designs/{id}/ops` by `id`, or by `ref` when it has one.

ref.description: The name it was added with.

drawnSize.description: The size the text is drawn at, when a fitting frame shrank it.

asset.description: The file or library graphic it shows.

tiles.description: How many tiles a pattern has.

field.description: Customers edit it in the form.

overflow.description: Its text does not fit its box.

DesignContent.title: DesignContent
DesignContent.description: What is on each page of a design. Boxes are `[x, y, width, height]` in `unit`, measured from the top-left of the trim (of the print area, on garment pages); text sizes are in points.

safeMargin.description: How far inside the trim the safe zone starts; null without one.

safeArea.description: The safe zone as [x, y, width, height] from the top-left of the trim: keep text and key artwork inside it.

printArea.description: The page is a garment mockup: boxes are measured from its print area.

panels.description: The panels of a folded page.

DesignCreate.title: DesignCreate
DesignCreate.description: A new design with blank pages.

unit.description: The unit for `width`, `height`, `bleed` and `safeMargin`, and the unit the design is measured in afterwards.

pageTitles.description: A title per page, for example `["Front", "Back"]`. Default *Page 1*, *Page 2*, …

bleed.description: Bleed on every edge, outside the trim.

safeMargin.description: Safe margin on every edge, inside the trim.

folderId.description: The design folder to create it in. Default `root`, the top level.

title.description: The copy's name. Default: the original's, with *(copy)*.

folderId.description: The folder to put the copy in. Default `root`.

parentId.description: The folder to create it in. Default `root`.

nextCursor.description: Pass as `cursor` to fetch the next page. `null` on the last page.

parentId.description: Move the folder into this one (`root` for the top level).

DesignFolder.title: DesignFolder
DesignFolder.description: A folder of designs. The top level is the folder `root`.

parentId.description: The folder it sits in; `null` for `root`.

DesignList.title: DesignList
DesignList.description: A page of designs, in id order.

nextCursor.description: Pass as `cursor` to fetch the next page. `null` on the last page.

Design.title: Design
Design.description: A design (template) your customers start from. Open it in the editor with `new PrintAppClient({ designId })`.

unit.description: The unit the design is measured in: `mm`, `cm`, `in`, `pt`, `px` or `ft`.

title.description: The page's name, when it has one (for example *Front*).

previewUrl.description: A preview image of the page.

Error.title: Error
Error.description: Every error the API itself returns. Match on `code`; `message` is for people and may be reworded.

code.description: `unauthorized` (401): missing, unknown, revoked or expired secret key. `account_suspended` (403): the account has an unpaid invoice. `invalid_request` (400): a parameter or body field is malformed — see `param` and `details`. `not_found` (404): no such resource in your account. `route_not_found` (404): no such endpoint. `idempotency_key_reused` (409): the Idempotency-Key was used for a different request. `idempotency_in_progress` (409): the first request with that key is still running. `folder_not_empty` (409): the folder still holds designs or folders. `builtin_folder`, `builtin_palette` (409): Print.App's own folders and palettes cannot be changed. `editor_not_supported` (409): page content can only be edited on accounts that use the new editor. `design_changed` (409): the design was saved elsewhere while the batch ran; read it again and retry. `payload_too_large` (413): a body or file over the limit. `unsupported_media_type` (415): send JSON. `ops_failed` (422): an operation in the batch failed, nothing was saved — see `details`. `internal_error` (500): retry; contact support with the `requestId` if it persists. `service_unavailable` (503): retry in a few seconds.

param.description: The parameter or body field at fault, as a path (`pages[0].title`).

details.description: Every problem found, when there was more than one (`invalid_request`), or each operation's result (`ops_failed`).

requestId.description: Also sent as the `x-request-id` header. Quote it when contacting support.

examples.message: limit must be an integer from 1 to 100.

FileCreate.title: FileCreate
FileCreate.description: A file to download from a public URL.

url.description: A public http(s) URL of a PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF, SVG, TIFF or PDF, up to 50 MB.

title.description: A name for the file. Default: from the URL.

folderId.description: A graphic folder to put it in.

nextCursor.description: Pass as `cursor` to fetch the next page. `null` on the last page.

FileUploadCreate.title: FileUploadCreate
FileUploadCreate.description: The file you are about to upload.

filename.description: The file's name, with its extension.

size.description: The file size in bytes, up to 200 MB. The upload is refused if the file is larger.

title.description: A name for the file. Default: the file name.

FileUpload.title: FileUpload
FileUpload.description: A presigned form for one direct upload.

fileId.description: The id the file will have once uploaded.

fields.description: Send every field, then the file last as `file`.

File.title: File
File.description: An image or graphic in your account.

id.description: Use it as `asset` in design operations.

FolderDesign.title: FolderDesign
FolderDesign.description: A design to put in the folder.

FolderFile.title: FolderFile
FolderFile.description: A file to put in the folder.

FontCreate.title: FontCreate
FontCreate.description: A Google font family to import, or a font file to upload. Send one of `family` or `url`.

family.description: A Google Fonts family name, for example `Playfair Display`. Every weight and style is imported.

url.description: A public URL of a TTF, OTF, WOFF or WOFF2 file, up to 20 MB. Its family, weight and style are read from the file.

nextCursor.description: Pass as `cursor` to fetch the next page. `null` on the last page.

family.description: The name to use in design operations (lower case).

panel.description: The editor panel that shows it.

nextCursor.description: Pass as `cursor` to fetch the next page. `null` on the last page.

fileIds.description: The folder's files in their new order: exactly the ids it holds now.

GraphicFolder.title: GraphicFolder
GraphicFolder.description: A folder of graphics in one of the editor's panels.

fileIds.description: Its files, in the order the editor shows them.

builtIn.description: Provided by Print.App: listed, but cannot be changed.

LinkCreate.title: LinkCreate
LinkCreate.description: What the link opens. Send one of `designId` or `projectId`.

projectId.description: A project to carry on with.

expiresAt.description: When the link stops working. Default: 30 days from now. At most a year.

userData.description: Your own details (customer, order), saved onto projects made through the link.

projectId.description: The project it opens, or the one a customer saved through it.

OpResult.title: OpResult
OpResult.description: One operation's result. Also the items of an error's `details` for `invalid_request` and `ops_failed` on `POST /v2/designs/{id}/ops`.

index.description: The operation's position in `ops`; null for a problem with the batch itself.

id.description: The id of the item it added or changed.

pageId.description: The id of the page it added.

path.description: The part of the operation at fault.

OpsBatch.title: OpsBatch
OpsBatch.description: A batch of design operations, run in order as one change: either every operation succeeds and the design is saved, or nothing is. Each operation is checked against its own schema (the DesignOp schemas) before anything runs.

units.description: The unit of every box and length in the batch. Default: the design's unit (mm for designs measured in ft). Text sizes are always in points.

page.description: The page item operations go on: a page number from 1, or a page's ref. An operation's own `page` wins. Default 1.

ops.description: The operations, run in order. Items added in the batch can be targeted by later operations through their `ref`.

dryRun.description: Run the batch and report every operation's result and the resulting content, without saving anything.

OpsResult.title: OpsResult
OpsResult.description: The outcome of a batch that ran: every operation's result, the design as saved (unchanged on a dry run), and its content now.

position.description: Move the page to this index.
The index the first new page takes. Default: after the last page.

name.description: The colour's name, shown in the editor.

cmyk.description: The print colour as `c,m,y,k` percentages, for example `0,16,100,0`.

spot.description: A spot colour name for print, for example `PANTONE 186 C`.

nextCursor.description: Pass as `cursor` to fetch the next page. `null` on the last page.

name.description: The colour's name, shown in the editor.

cmyk.description: The print colour as `c,m,y,k` percentages, for example `0,16,100,0`.

spot.description: A spot colour name for print, for example `PANTONE 186 C`.

builtIn.description: Provided by Print.App: it cannot be changed, only hidden by deleting it.

ProductList.title: ProductList
ProductList.description: A page of products, in id order.

nextCursor.description: Pass as `cursor` to fetch the next page. `null` on the last page.

title.description: The product's name, shown in the dashboard. Default: the current one, or the product id.

designIds.description: The designs the product opens, in order. `[]` leaves only the variants' designs.

id.description: The variant's id in your store.

designIds.description: The designs this variant opens instead of the product's.

variants.description: Per-variant designs. Variants you leave out open the product's designs.

Product.title: Product
Product.description: The designs one store product opens.

id.description: The product's id in your store.

ProjectList.title: ProjectList
ProjectList.description: A page of projects, most recently modified first.

hasMore.description: Whether another page may follow. A following page can come back empty when a `status` filter excludes the remaining projects.

nextCursor.description: Pass as `cursor` to fetch the next page, with the same filters. `null` on the last page.

userData.description: Merged into the project's `userData`, one level deep. A key set to `null` is removed.

status.description: `submitted`: the customer finished the design (the editor's submit). `saved`: saved for later. `draft`: autosaved, not yet saved by the customer.

product.description: Exactly the `product` object your page passed to `PrintAppClient` when the project was created — for example `{ id, ref }`. Use it to check the project was made for the product being ordered. It passes through the customer's browser, so treat it as the customer's claim about the page, not as proof.

userId.description: The `userId` your page passed to `PrintAppClient`, if any.

userData.description: Customer details attached to the project by a store plugin or your page: `id`, `name`, `email`, `phone`, `info`.

designId.description: The design (template) the project was made from.

previewUrl.description: A preview image of the page.

exports.description: Print files, rendered on request from the project's current state.

DesignOpPartRef.description: A short name you choose; later ops (and later batches) can target the item by it.

DesignOpPartTarget.description: An item ref or item id.

DesignOpPartBox.description: [x, y, width, height] from the trim top-left (the print window's on garment pages).

DesignOpPartAsset.description: One of your file ids (file_…) or a print.app library graphic id (c_…). An SVG file stays vector in print.

DesignOpPartSvg.description: SVG markup, inline. Through the API, upload SVGs as files instead (POST /v2/files or /v2/files/uploads) and place them with `asset`: the firewall in front of api.print.app refuses request bodies that carry markup, with an HTML 403.

DesignOpPartSvgPath.description: SVG path data drawn in a 0..1 box, stretched to the box.

DesignOpPartFont.description: A font family name from the account's fonts (GET /v2/fonts).

template.description: Smart tokens: "{Phone | type: tel, default: +1 555 0100}"; each token is a form field.

leading.description: Line spacing as a multiple of size.

params.description: Per type, as playbook/ops.md module.add (colours hex, fonts family names, sizes pt, lengths in the batch units, motifs as asset ids).

position.description: 1-based index to insert at (default: the end). The new page copies the first page's size, bleed and margin.

DesignOpItemUpdate.title: item.update
DesignOpItemUpdate.description: Changes an item. Items added earlier in the same batch take any property of the op that added them. Items already on the saved design take: box, content, font, size, weight, style, color, leading, tracking, align, anchor, fill, stroke, opacity, rotate, lock, field, asset, svg, cornerRadius.

to.description: safe, page, panel or a ref (default: the first target).

GatewayError.description: Returned by the API gateway itself (429).
